initial_description:
Here is a detailed description of the illustrative figure representing the LoRA adaptation of the DistilBERT encoder, designed for a clean, academic publication style.

### 1. Overall Layout
The diagram follows a left-to-right horizontal flow divided into three primary vertical zones, with an additional horizontal annotation strip running along the bottom. 
*   **Zone 1 (Far Left):** The input section.
*   **Zone 2 (Middle Left):** The frozen encoder stack.
*   **Zone 3 (Right):** An enlarged "zoom-in" callout detailing the attention projection, followed by the classification head and the final output.
*   **Bottom Section:** A horizontal bracket strip providing context for the bracketing baselines.

### 2. Components
*   **Input Module:** A rounded rectangle labeled exactly "**Input text**" with a smaller subtitle below it reading "**a charming film**".
*   **Encoder Container:** A tall rounded rectangle acting as a container. The title above it reads "**DistilBERT encoder (frozen)**", accompanied by a small padlock icon (without a snowflake) to visually indicate that the weights are locked/frozen.
*   **Transformer Layers:** Inside the Encoder Container, there is a vertical stack of six identical, thin rounded bars. They are labeled "**Transformer layer**" and numbered 1 through 6 from top to bottom.
*   **Zoom-in Callout (Attention Projection):** A large rounded rectangle to the right of the encoder. It has the title "**Attention projection**". Inside this callout:
    *   On the left: A square labeled "**W0 frozen**".
    *   In the middle: A bold "**+**" (plus) sign.
    *   On the right: Two small, vertically stacked rectangles. The top one is labeled "**B**" and the bottom one is labeled "**A**". These are drawn noticeably smaller to visually represent their low-rank nature. Beside them is a short caption: "**trainable low-rank update**".
*   **Classification Head:** To the right of the zoom-in callout, a rounded rectangle labeled "**Classification head (trainable)**".
*   **Output:** At the far right end, a simple text label reading "**class**".
*   **Baseline Bracket Strip:** A thin horizontal strip running along the bottom of the entire figure. It contains two italicized captions. The left side reads "**rank-0 probe = head only (encoder frozen)**", and the right side reads "**full fine-tuning = all weights trainable**".

### 3. Connections
*   **Main Data Flow:** Solid black arrows connect the main sequence: Input Module $\rightarrow$ Encoder Container $\rightarrow$ Zoom-in Callout $\rightarrow$ Classification Head $\rightarrow$ "class" output.
*   **Zoom Indicator:** Thin, dotted lines connect the side of the Encoder Container to the large Zoom-in Callout, visually indicating that the callout is an expanded view of the internal attention mechanism.
*   **Internal Callout Flow:** Inside the Zoom-in Callout, a short arrow points from the low-rank branch (matrices B and A) into the bold "+" sign, showing the addition of the trainable update to the frozen weights.

### 4. Groupings
*   The six "Transformer layer" bars are strictly contained within the boundaries of the "DistilBERT encoder (frozen)" container.
*   The frozen weight square ("W0 frozen"), the addition operator ("+"), and the low-rank matrices ("A" and "B") are grouped together inside the "Attention projection" zoom-in callout boundary.

### 5. Labels and Annotations
*   All text labels are plain, sans-serif font. No mathematical formulas or equations are used other than the simple "W0", "A", and "B" matrix designations.
*   Titles and module names (e.g., "Attention projection", "Classification head (trainable)") are clear and prominently placed either inside or just above their respective bounding boxes.
*   The bottom bracket strip uses italicized text to differentiate it from the structural module labels.

### 6. Input/Output
*   **Input:** Raw text data (represented by the phrase "a charming film") enters the system on the far left.
*   **Output:** The final classification prediction (represented by the word "class") exits the system on the far right.

### 7. Styling
*   **Background:** Pure white, completely flat. No gray tints, gradients, or background clutter.
*   **Color Palette (Pastel & Academic):**
    *   *Input Module:* Light gray fill.
    *   *Encoder Container:* Very light pastel blue fill with a slightly darker, solid blue border.
    *   *Transformer Layers:* Pale sky blue fill.
    *   *Zoom-in Callout:* White fill with a light gray border.
    *   *Frozen Weight (W0):* Medium gray fill.
    *   *Low-Rank Matrices (A & B):* Soft coral/peach fill with a slightly darker coral border. The accompanying text ("trainable low-rank update") and arrow are also in matching coral to establish a visual connection.
    *   *Classification Head:* Pale mint green fill with a darker, solid green border.
    *   *Bottom Bracket Strip:* Very light off-white/gray.
*   **Linework & Formatting:** Clean, flat design. Borders are thin (1-2px) and solid, except for the dotted zoom-in lines. Corners of the rectangles are subtly rounded. There are absolutely no drop shadows or 3D effects. Generous spacing is maintained between all elements to ensure publication-level clarity.

*   Typography strictly follows academic conventions: clean sans-serif (e.g., Helvetica or Roboto) for all structural labels and headers, with bolding used for primary titles. Variables (*W0*, *A*, *B*) use an italicized serif font to mimic LaTeX styling.

Corners of the process nodes and containers are subtly softened/rounded, while data matrices (W0, A, B) retain sharper, square corners to denote data structures. There are absolutely no drop shadows or 3D effects, ensuring a highly polished, publication-ready aesthetic suitable for top-tier AI conferences.
